I've attached our rough usage CSV. Can you send a simple proforma for 12- and 24-month commitments with staged discounts, and a plain-language fallback clause we can show procurement?

Attachments: proforma_reserve_options.pdf, commit_scenarios.xlsx (calc tabs). Please reply with redlines in-line — we need final language to send to PilotHealth on Monday.

Irene — thanks for the modeling. A few points from Finance/RevOps POV: 
- We can accept a capped escalation tied to a third-party GPU index but it must be bounded. Propose: index trigger bands (0–10% no change, 10–20% -> one-time protection credit; >20% -> exec review). No automatic discount increases beyond 12% without SLT signoff.
- Fallback/burst to Hosted at a capped rate is fine for short provisioning windows, but reduce the cap window to 20% of monthly committed units; anything beyond should be charged at list hosted rate and we owe a credit only if the miss is operational (not customer over-usage).
- For 24-month deals where they request a 20% discount floor, that requires Sales Director + CFO approval.

Operational asks: David — ops needs a clear SLA checklist to certify region availability before committing to 24m. Karhtik/Karthik — queue for legal to draft fallback language that matches the above.

My recommend: present PilotHealth with two clean options: 12m (12% max discount, 20% burst cap at $0.0042/unit with credit if miss is ops) and 24m (14% standard discount, 18% with exec approval, stricter SLA acceptance). If they push for more, we ask for a higher commitment or price protection escrow.

Marissa

Avery — thanks for the patience. Per internal review we've prepared a concise proposal and fallback language. High level: 

Option A — 12 months (standard):
- Committed: 63M units/month
- Max standard discount: 12%
- Burst fallback: up to 20% of monthly committed units can burst to Redwood Hosted at $0.0042/unit during provisioning shortfalls; operational misses (Redwood responsibility) trigger a credit equal to 50% of the overage delta for the affected month.

Option B — 24 months (expanded):
- Committed: same monthly units, 24m term
- Standard discount: 14% (up to 18% with exec approval)
- SLA acceptance required prior to signing; for discounts above 14% Exec approval required.

GPU cost sensitivity and index: we will not automatically increase discounts if third-party GPU indexes rise; instead we offer a bounded protection mechanism: if the index increases by 10–20% versus baseline, PilotHealth receives a one-time credit structure (outlined in the attached proposal); >20% triggers a joint executive review to agree remedial actions. This avoids open-ended passthroughs while giving procurement certainty.

Attached: pilothealth_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal summary + plain-language fallback clause).
